paper.title: Cooperation prevails when individuals adjust their social ties

headline: Santos-Pacheco-Lenaerts 2006 coevolving-network PD (agent-based): 1/3 locked clauses REPRO; b/c=2 static graph collapses (coop=0.000 at W=0) while adaptive rewiring rescues cooperation (coop=0.630 at W=16)

verdicts.gate: P1 static graph (W=0) collapses: mean steady cooperation < 0.05 at b/c=2 on the homogeneous random graph
P2 coevolution prevails (W=16): mean steady cooperation > 0.80 AND enhancement over the static graph > 0.6
reasons: W=16 mean steady cooperation = 0.6302 (need > 0.8); enhancement over W=0 = 0.6302 (need > 0.6)

verdicts.gate: P3 monotone W-dependence with a threshold: coop(16)-coop(0.5) > 0.5, coop(0.5) < 0.2, coop(16) > 0.7

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the coevolution-rescues-cooperation effect (and isolate rewiring as its cause via the W=0 control), and would catch an artifact. Framing: network-generation + adaptive rewiring (disclosed).

citations: Santos, F.C., Pacheco, J.M. & Lenaerts, T. (2006). Cooperation prevails when individuals adjust their social ties. PLoS Computational Biology 2(10):e140. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.0020140.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the steady-state cooperator fraction versus the timescale ratio W
